limitations: These are large, highly ranked sites, not small businesses. A figure here is not a statement about a small company's robots.txt.

READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING A PERCENTAGE. Only 407 of 700 requested robots.txt files could be read; 145 answered 403 to this measurement's client. Hosts that refuse an unknown automated client are plausibly the same hosts that restrict AI crawlers, so the read subset probably UNDER-states blocking. Every requested domain is in the sites list with the reason it could not be read, so the gap is auditable rather than hidden.

A block is not necessarily a mistake. Some publishers restrict OAI-SearchBot deliberately while negotiating licensing. That is why each verdict records whether the governing group names the crawler (a deliberate rule) or is the blanket "*" group (a rule inherited by every bot alike), and the two are counted separately below.
